diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw the five parenthesizations of g,h,k,l,m as vertices and the elementary associator/pentagonator transitions as directed edges; annotate the two boundary routes with the exact scalar products in line 52 and state their equality by line 38. diagram_candidates.source_claim: For composable bimodules X:A→B, Y:B→D, Z:D→E, either parenthesized iterated balanced tensor product represents the same functor; for four composable bimodules the two associator composites preserve the same universal four-balanced map, so uniqueness gives the pentagon.
diagram_candidates.why: The theorem explicitly asserts bicategory pentagon coherence and its proof invokes two paths around the pentagon, but presents the comparison only in prose. A small diagram would expose the associator direction and routes.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Use four composable bimodules and vertices (((X⊗_B Y)⊗_D Z)⊗_E W), (X⊗_B(Y⊗_D Z))⊗_E W, (X⊗_B Y)⊗_D(Z⊗_E W), X⊗_B((Y⊗_D Z)⊗_E W), and X⊗_B(Y⊗_D(Z⊗_E W)); label the five edges with the canonical associators in the stated direction and compare the two paths. The proof says both preserve the universal four-balanced map; make clear that the diagram is a coherence comparison and does not add hypotheses.
